skills.name: Factorials & counting
skills.wrong_turn: A factorial ratio cancels, it doesn't divide the numbers. (6!3!)=6×5×4=120, not 2!=2.

skills.name: Permutations
skills.wrong_turn: Repeated letters don't make new words. BOOK has 4!/2! = 12 arrangements, not 4! = 24: swapping the two O's changes nothing.

skills.name: Combinations
skills.wrong_turn: If order doesn't matter, don't use nPr. A 3-person committee from 10 people is ((103))=120, not 10P3=720.

skills.name: Counting with conditions
skills.wrong_turn: Don't count “at least one” by fixing one and choosing the rest freely. From 4 boys and 5 girls, 3-person committees with at least one girl number 84−4=80, not 5×((82))=140, which counts some committees twice or more.

skills.name: Probability by counting
skills.wrong_turn: Outcomes must be equally likely. Two dice have 11 possible sums, but P(sum 7)=(636)=(16), not (111).

skills.name: Addition rule
skills.wrong_turn: Don't just add when events overlap. P(heart or king)=(1352)+(452)−(152)=(1652), not (1752).

skills.name: Complements & "at least one"

steps.b: at least one, by the complement

skills.wrong_turn: Don't multiply the single chance by the number of tries. At least one six in 4 rolls is 1−((56))4≈0.518, not 4×(16)=(23).

skills.name: Independent events
skills.wrong_turn: Independent is not the same as mutually exclusive. If A and B can't both happen, with P(A)=0.5 and P(B)=0.4, then P(A∩B)=0, not 0.2: they are dependent.

skills.name: Conditional probability
skills.wrong_turn: Don't flip the condition. If 12 of 30 athletes are seniors and there are 40 seniors, P(senior∣athlete)=(1230)=0.4, but P(athlete∣senior)=(1240)=0.3.

skills.name: Tree diagrams
skills.wrong_turn: Multiply along a branch, add across paths. Two reds from 3 red and 2 blue without replacement is (35)×(24)=(310), not (35)+(24).

skills.name: Bayes' theorem

steps.d: with a tree or a table

skills.wrong_turn: Don't confuse P(sick given positive) with P(positive given sick). A test that is 99% right both ways, for a disease 1 in 1000 people have, gives positives that are right only about 9% of the time.

skills.name: Expected value
skills.wrong_turn: Expected value is a weighted average, not a plain average of the outcomes. A game paying 10 dollars with chance 0.1 and nothing otherwise is worth 1 dollar, not (10 + 0)/2 = 5 dollars.
